module purpose: neorv32_uart is a bus-attached UART: a control word written over bus_req_i is held in ctrl (enable, simulation mode, flow-control enable, prescaler select, baud divisor, interrupt enables, FIFO clear requests); bytes written to the data address enter a TX FIFO sub-unit, are framed and shifted out on uart_txd_o, while uart_rxd_i is synchronized, sampled and deserialized into an RX FIFO sub-unit that is read back over bus_rsp_o. It also drives uart_rtsn_o, reads uart_ctsn_i, raises irq_rx_o and irq_tx_o, and exports clkgen_en_o.

use-case flows.value: control word (enable, simulation mode, flow-control enable, prescaler select, baud divisor, interrupt enables, FIFO clear requests) taken from bus write data into ctrl on a write to the control address
transmit byte pushed into the TX FIFO by a bus write to the data address
one-cycle FIFO clear request and the resulting clear decision for each FIFO
bit timing: prescaler tick selected from clkgen_i by ctrl.prsc, clock-generator enable exported
transmission: byte fetched from the TX FIFO, framed with start and stop bits, shifted out on uart_txd_o at the baud rate, start held by CTS when flow control is on
reception: uart_rxd_i synchronized, start edge detected, bits sampled and shifted in, completed byte written into the RX FIFO
flow control: RTS driven from enable and RX FIFO half-full when hardware flow control is on
simulation output: in builds where sim_mode_en_c is true and simulation mode is set, a bus write to the data address is printed to the simulator output and log file
interrupt requests computed from FIFO status and interrupt enables
status: FIFO levels, receive overrun flag, transmitter busy
control settings and received bytes returned on a bus read
ctrl, engine registers, overrun flag, interrupts and RTS forced to constants while rstn_i is low; FIFOs held clear and overrun flag cleared while ctrl.enable is 0

conceptual assets.concept: UART enable setting -- whether the engines, FIFOs, interrupts and the external clock generator are active
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow writes it: `ctrl.enable <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_en_c);` (line 179, CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, under the write predicates of lines 176-178). The module's behavior depends on it: while 0 both FIFOs are held cleared (lines 259, 304, GATES tx_fifo.clear / rx_fifo.clear), both interrupt outputs are forced to 0 (lines 270, 315), the overrun flag is cleared (lines 458-459), RTS is forced high when flow control is on (lines 472-475), and the top state bit of each engine copies it (lines 344, 417), so an engine leaves idle only when enabled (lines 347, 420). It leaves the entity through `clkgen_en_o <= ctrl.enable;` (line 228, COPIES ctrl.enable), whose consumer is not supplied, so integrity of the delivered value is Established. Availability is also Established: clearing it stops transmit, receive and interrupts (lines 259, 304, 270, 315). No line restricts readback (line 195), so confidentiality is not established. bus_req_i and bus_rsp_o are transport records (address, data, strobe, rw, ack, err), so they are neither setting point nor exit; tx_engine.state and rx_engine.state copy only one bit of it and are listed under their own sequencing concepts.

conceptual assets.concept: Serial bit-rate configuration -- prescaler tick selection and baud divisor that time every transmitted and received bit
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow holds `ctrl.prsc <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_prsc2_c downto ctrl_prsc0_c);` (line 182) and `ctrl.baud <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_baud9_c downto ctrl_baud0_c);` (line 183), each CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3. ctrl.prsc selects the tick `uart_clk <= clkgen_i(to_integer(unsigned(ctrl.prsc)));` (line 229, SELECTS uart_clk), and every engine step waits for that tick (lines 358, 366, 409, 430). ctrl.baud reloads both bit-period counters (lines 349, 368, 432, CARRIES) and sets the half-bit start offset (line 422, SOURCES rx_engine.baudcnt), a computation in this entity that reads the setting. Integrity: a corrupted value changes the bit period of every transmitted and received frame, so the serial line no longer follows the configured rate. Availability: the period is held between writes. uart_clk only routes one bit of clkgen_i (line 229); clkgen_i is a clock-enable input that only enables engine steps, so neither is listed. Readback (lines 198-199) leaves through the transport record bus_rsp_o.

conceptual assets.concept: Hardware flow-control enable setting -- whether transmission obeys CTS and RTS reports receive readiness
conceptual assets.reasoning: Written by `ctrl.hwfc_en <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_hwfc_en_c);` (line 181, CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3). It decides whether a frame waits for CTS: `if (uart_clk = '1') and ((tx_engine.cts(1) = '0') or (ctrl.hwfc_en = '0'))` (lines 358-359, GATES tx_engine.state), and whether RTS follows the receive state or is held at 0 (lines 472-480, GATES uart_rtsn_o). Integrity: a wrong value makes the transmitter ignore or honor CTS and makes RTS report a readiness other than configured. Availability: when set while CTS stays high, a frame never leaves the wait state (line 360). Readback (line 197) is through the transport record.

conceptual assets.concept: Simulation-mode setting -- whether serial traffic is suppressed and data-register writes are diverted to the simulator log
conceptual assets.reasoning: Written by `ctrl.sim_mode <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_sim_en_c) and bool_to_ulogic_f(sim_mode_en_c);` (line 180, CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3), with `sim_mode_en_c := SIM_MODE_EN and is_simulation_c` (line 50). Build condition: only where sim_mode_en_c is true can it become 1; otherwise every write gives 0 and it stays at its reset value 0 (line 157). When 1, both FIFOs are held cleared (lines 259, 304, GATES tx_fifo.clear / rx_fifo.clear), so no byte is transmitted or received, and in those builds a bus write to the data address is printed to the simulator output instead (lines 491, 499-511). Integrity: its value decides whether data goes to the serial line or is diverted. Availability: setting it stops both serial flows. The map lists it as a control-only source; the RTL agrees that it is used only in conditions.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt condition enables -- which FIFO conditions are allowed to raise each interrupt
conceptual assets.reasoning: Five settings are written at lines 185-189 (each CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3) and read by the interrupt computations: `irq_rx_o <= ctrl.enable and ((ctrl.irq_rx_nempty and rx_fifo.avail) or (ctrl.irq_rx_half and rx_fifo.half) or (ctrl.irq_rx_full and (not rx_fifo.free)));` (lines 315-318) and `irq_tx_o <= ctrl.enable and ((ctrl.irq_tx_empty and (not tx_fifo.avail)) or (ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf and (not tx_fifo.half)));` (lines 270-272); each SOURCES its interrupt output port. Integrity: a corrupted enable raises or suppresses an interrupt contrary to the configuration. Availability: a cleared enable suppresses the event. Readback (lines 208-212) is through the transport record.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt requests -- the receive and transmit interrupt events delivered to the system
conceptual assets.reasoning: The report flow computes and registers each request (lines 270-272 and 315-318, DERIVES_FROM the enables and FIFO status, GATED_BY ctrl.enable at occurrence 3), resets it to 0 (lines 268, 313), and drives it out of the entity, where its consumer is not supplied: integrity that the consumer receives exactly the condition these lines define is Established. Availability: the request is produced at each clock edge while its condition holds and the module is enabled. Both ports use exit port ahead of their overlapping storage. The FIFO status fields rx_fifo.avail, rx_fifo.half, rx_fifo.free, tx_fifo.avail and tx_fifo.half only receive sub-unit outputs (lines 247, 256, 292, 297, 301) and are operands here, not listed.

conceptual assets.concept: FIFO flush decision -- the request and the computed decision that discard the contents of each FIFO
conceptual assets.reasoning: A control write with the clear bits set pulses `ctrl.clr_rx <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_rx_clr_c);` / `ctrl.clr_tx <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_tx_clr_c);` (lines 190-191, CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4), cleared again on the next edge (lines 173-174). The decision is computed here: `tx_fifo.clear <= '1' when (ctrl.enable = '0') or (ctrl.sim_mode = '1') or (ctrl.clr_tx = '1') else '0';` (line 259) and its RX counterpart (line 304), and wired to the clear inputs of the FIFO sub-units (lines 246, 291), whose internals are not supplied: integrity that each FIFO receives exactly this decision is Established. Availability: a spurious clear discards queued bytes. ctrl.clr_tx and ctrl.clr_rx store the request (GATES the clear fields); tx_fifo.clear and rx_fifo.clear compute the decision (GATED_BY at occurrence 3), so the sub-unit wiring exception (computed here from a decision) is met. ctrl.enable and ctrl.sim_mode are operands that realize their own concepts.

conceptual assets.concept: FIFO push and pop decisions -- when a byte is written into or taken from each FIFO
conceptual assets.reasoning: Four strobes are decided in this entity and delivered to FIFO sub-units that are not supplied: the bus-side push `tx_fifo.we <= '1' when (bus_req_i.stb = '1') and (bus_req_i.rw = '1') and (bus_req_i.addr(2) = '1') else '0';` (line 261, to we_i at line 251), the bus-side pop `rx_fifo.re` (line 307, to re_i at line 299), the engine-side fetch `tx_fifo.re <= '1' when (tx_engine.state = 100) else '0';` (line 262, to re_i at line 254), and the receive-complete event `rx_engine.done <= '1'` when the bit counter reaches 0 in the sampling state (line 440, GATED_BY rx_engine.bitcnt at occurrence 5), which reaches we_i through line 306 and line 296. Integrity that each FIFO receives exactly these strobes is Established; a wrong strobe drops, duplicates or loses bytes. Availability: without the strobes no byte enters or leaves a FIFO. The three fifo fields are computed here from decisions, so the sub-unit wiring exception is met. rx_fifo.we is a combinational copy of rx_engine.done (COPIES, line 306), so rx_engine.done is kept; it is also the overrun condition operand at line 460.

conceptual assets.concept: Transmitter frame sequencing state -- engine state, bit count and bit-period count of the frame being sent
conceptual assets.reasoning: The transmit flow is sequenced by `case tx_engine.state is` (line 345): fetch and load (lines 347-353), wait for tick and CTS (lines 356-360), shift (lines 363-377), back to idle (line 382). tx_engine.bitcnt is loaded (line 350), decremented (line 369) and ends the frame (lines 375-377, GATES tx_engine.state); tx_engine.baudcnt is loaded from ctrl.baud (lines 349, 368), counts down (line 372) and decides each shift (line 367, GATES tx_engine.bitcnt and tx_engine.sreg). All three are self-updating registers (CLOCKED_BY clk_i). Integrity: corrupted state or counts produce missing or extra bits, a wrong bit period, or skipped bytes. Availability: a stuck state stops transmission. tx_engine.done is assigned (lines 340, 376) but never read, so it has no local use and is not listed.

conceptual assets.concept: Transmitted serial data -- the framed bit stream driven on the transmit line
conceptual assets.reasoning: `tx_engine.sreg <= tx_fifo.rdata & '0';` (line 351) loads the byte with a start bit, line 370 shifts in stop bits, `tx_engine.txd <= tx_engine.sreg(0);` (line 365) drives each bit with idle level 1 (line 341), and `uart_txd_o <= tx_engine.txd;` (line 392) delivers it to a consumer outside the entity: integrity that the line carries exactly the framed byte is Established. Availability: the bit is driven at every clock edge. tx_engine.txd stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4, CARRIES uart_txd_o); uart_txd_o is the exit port. tx_engine.sreg's records show data only to tx_engine.txd and itself (lines 365, 370), so it holds one step of a value that tx_engine.txd carries on and is secondary. tx_fifo.rdata only receives the sub-unit output (line 255) and tx_fifo.wdata only passes bus write data to the sub-unit (lines 250, 260): both are carriers. The map lists tx_engine.txd and uart_txd_o as not reached from a source because the data passes through the FIFO sub-unit.

conceptual assets.concept: Receiver frame sequencing state -- engine state, bit count and bit-period count of the frame being received
conceptual assets.reasoning: The receive flow is sequenced by `case rx_engine.state is` (line 418): wait for the start edge (lines 420-425), sample (lines 428-441), idle when disabled (line 446). rx_engine.baudcnt starts at half a bit period (line 422), reloads (line 432), counts down (line 436) and decides each sample (line 431, GATES rx_engine.bitcnt and rx_engine.sreg); rx_engine.bitcnt is loaded (line 423), decremented (line 433) and ends the frame (lines 439-441, GATES rx_engine.done and rx_engine.state). All three are self-updating registers (CLOCKED_BY clk_i). Integrity: corrupted state or counts misframe bytes or sample at wrong points. Availability: a stuck state stops reception.

conceptual assets.concept: Received serial data -- the receive line value sampled into the module
conceptual assets.reasoning: This entity reads uart_rxd_i to store it: `rx_engine.sync(2) <= uart_rxd_i;` (line 408, CARRIES rx_engine.sync at occurrence 2). rx_engine.sync shifts on each tick (line 410), its low bits decide the start edge (line 424, GATES rx_engine.state) and sync(2) is sampled into the received byte (line 434). Integrity: corruption of the sampled line changes the received byte and the frame timing. Availability: sampling happens at every clock edge. rx_engine.sync stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3). Mapping limitation: rx_engine.sreg assembles the byte (line 434), but its records show only SOURCES rx_fifo.wdata (line 305) and itself, both internal, so under the storing rule it is secondary; rx_fifo.wdata passes sreg(7 downto 0) unchanged to the sub-unit input (line 295) and rx_fifo.rdata only receives the sub-unit output (line 300) and leaves through the transport record (line 217), so both are carriers. The stored received byte therefore has no eligible reference in this entity beyond the sampled line.

conceptual assets.concept: Clear-to-send permission -- the link partner's CTS level that allows a frame to start
conceptual assets.reasoning: This entity reads uart_ctsn_i into a two-stage register: `tx_engine.cts <= tx_engine.cts(0) & uart_ctsn_i;` (line 337, SOURCES tx_engine.cts at occurrence 2). tx_engine.cts(1) decides whether a frame may start when flow control is on (lines 358-360, GATES tx_engine.state). Integrity: the transmitter must start only when the synchronized CTS permits. Availability: a CTS held high blocks transmission while ctrl.hwfc_en is 1. tx_engine.cts stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3); it updates itself and is not a copy.

conceptual assets.concept: Request-to-send output -- the receive-readiness decision signalled to the link partner
conceptual assets.reasoning: The registered decision `if (ctrl.hwfc_en = '1') then if (ctrl.enable = '0') or (rx_fifo.half = '1') then uart_rtsn_o <= '1'; else uart_rtsn_o <= '0';` with 0 when flow control is off (lines 472-480, GATED_BY ctrl.hwfc_en at occurrence 3) leaves the entity to a consumer that is not supplied: integrity that the partner receives exactly this decision is Established. Availability: it is refreshed at every clock edge and reset to 0 (line 470). rx_fifo.half is a sub-unit output tested at line 474, but it is an operand of this decision, not its result, so it is not listed.

conceptual assets.concept: Receive overrun error flag -- set when a received byte is written into a full RX FIFO
conceptual assets.reasoning: `elsif (rx_fifo.we = '1') and (rx_fifo.free = '0') then rx_engine.over <= '1';` (lines 460-461, CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 5) sets the flag, it is cleared while the module is disabled (lines 458-459) and reported by `bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_rx_over_c) <= rx_engine.over;` (line 214, CARRIES into an output field of this entity). Integrity: the reported flag must reflect a write to a full FIFO, so a lost byte is visible. Availability: the flag holds until the module is disabled. rx_fifo.we and rx_fifo.free are operands of the condition, not its result.

conceptual assets.concept: Transmitter busy status -- whether the transmit engine is inside a frame, as reported to the bus requester
conceptual assets.reasoning: `tx_engine.busy <= '0' when (tx_engine.state(1 downto 0) = 00) else '1';` (line 389, GATED_BY tx_engine.state at occurrence 3) computes the decision, and `bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_tx_busy_c) <= tx_engine.busy or tx_fifo.avail;` (line 215, GATES bus_rsp_o.data) reports it out of the entity: integrity that the requester receives exactly this status is Established. Availability: it is computed continuously from the engine state. The exit is the transport record bus_rsp_o, which is not listed.
